#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""DisPeD Architecture Diagram — v5. Fixes output box text overlap.
Designed for figure* at \\textwidth ≈ 6.3in."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import FancyBboxPatch, FancyArrowPatch
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe

plt.rcParams.update({
    'pdf.fonttype': 42, 'ps.fonttype': 42,
    'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans',
})

C_BG     = "#FFFFFF"
C_BLUE   = "#0072B2"
C_CORAL  = "#D55E00"
C_TEAL   = "#009E73"
C_PURPLE = "#7B68AE"
C_DARK   = "#333333"
C_GRAY   = "#888888"

shadow_kw = [pe.withSimplePatchShadow(offset=(0.15, -0.15),
             shadow_rgbFace="#cccccc", alpha=0.06)]

W, H = 6.5, 2.8
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(W, H), dpi=300)
ax.set_xlim(0, W)
ax.set_ylim(0, H)
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.axis("off")
fig.patch.set_facecolor(C_BG)

def rbox(x, y, w, h, fc, ec="#CCC", lw=0.5, z=2, alpha=1, rad=0.05, shd=True):
    b = FancyBboxPatch((x, y), w, h, boxstyle=f"round,pad={rad}",
        fc=fc, ec=ec, lw=lw, zorder=z, alpha=alpha)
    if shd:
        b.set_path_effects(shadow_kw)
    ax.add_patch(b)

def arr(x1, y1, x2, y2, c=C_DARK, lw=0.5, style="-|>", z=5):
    ax.add_patch(FancyArrowPatch((x1, y1), (x2, y2), arrowstyle=style,
        color=c, lw=lw, mutation_scale=6, zorder=z))

ROW_Y = [2.10, 1.28, 0.46]

# ── Zone backgrounds ──
rbox(1.18, 0.10, 2.10, 2.52, fc="#F0F6FC", ec="#D0DFEE", lw=0.3,
     z=0, rad=0.10, alpha=0.45, shd=False)
rbox(3.42, 0.10, 2.98, 2.52, fc="#F6F0FC", ec="#DFD0EE", lw=0.3,
     z=0, rad=0.10, alpha=0.35, shd=False)

# ── Stage titles ──
ax.text(2.23, 2.72, "Stage 1: Encoder Adaptation", fontsize=8,
        fontweight="bold", color="#333", ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)
ax.text(4.95, 2.72, "Stage 2: Temporal Classification", fontsize=8,
        fontweight="bold", color="#333", ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)

# ── Chat bubbles ──
bx, bw, bh = 0.12, 0.82, 0.34
bubbles = [
    ("Can you help me\nwith chemistry...",  "User₁", ROW_Y[0]),
    ("Try a different\nangle...",           "User₂", ROW_Y[1]),
    ("Give me the\nfull recipe...",         "Userₖ", ROW_Y[2]),
]

for txt, lbl, cy in bubbles:
    by = cy - bh / 2
    bb = FancyBboxPatch((bx, by), bw, bh, boxstyle="round,pad=0.04",
        fc="#FAFBFC", ec="#D8DDE3", lw=0.4, zorder=3)
    bb.set_path_effects(shadow_kw)
    ax.add_patch(bb)
    tx = bx - 0.005
    ty = by + bh * 0.4
    ax.add_patch(plt.Polygon([(tx, ty + 0.025), (tx - 0.035, ty), (tx, ty - 0.025)],
        closed=True, fc="#FAFBFC", ec="#D8DDE3", lw=0.3, zorder=3))
    ax.text(bx - 0.07, cy, lbl, fontsize=6, fontweight="bold",
            color="#444", ha="right", va="center", zorder=5)
    ax.text(bx + bw / 2, cy, txt, fontsize=5, color="#999",
            ha="center", va="center", style="italic", zorder=5, linespacing=1.15)

ax.text(bx + bw / 2, (ROW_Y[1] + ROW_Y[2]) / 2, "⋮", fontsize=9,
        color=C_DARK, ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)

# ── DeBERTa encoders ──
ex, ew, eh = 1.38, 0.85, 0.38
enc_ys = [ROW_Y[i] - eh / 2 for i in range(3)]

for ey in enc_ys:
    rbox(ex, ey, ew, eh, fc="#E8F0F8", ec=C_BLUE, lw=0.6, z=3)
    ax.text(ex + ew / 2, ey + eh * 0.6, "DeBERTa", fontsize=7, fontweight="bold",
            color=C_BLUE, ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)
    for j in range(2):
        ly = ey + 0.04 + j * 0.10
        fills = ["#D6E6F5", "#AECEE8"]
        ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((ex + 0.08, ly), ew - 0.16, 0.06,
            boxstyle="round,pad=0.01", fc=fills[j], ec="#8AB6D8", lw=0.2, zorder=4))

bk_x = ex - 0.04
for i in range(2):
    y_bot = enc_ys[i + 1] + eh + 0.02
    y_top = enc_ys[i] - 0.02
    ax.plot([bk_x, bk_x], [y_bot, y_top], color=C_GRAY, lw=0.4,
            ls=(0, (2, 1.5)), zorder=2)
    ax.plot([bk_x - 0.03, bk_x + 0.03], [y_bot, y_bot], color=C_GRAY, lw=0.4, zorder=2)
    ax.plot([bk_x - 0.03, bk_x + 0.03], [y_top, y_top], color=C_GRAY, lw=0.4, zorder=2)

ax.text(ex - 0.12, ROW_Y[1], "shared\nweights", fontsize=4.5, color=C_GRAY,
        ha="right", va="center", style="italic", linespacing=1.1, zorder=5)

for i in range(3):
    arr(bx + bw + 0.02, ROW_Y[i], ex - 0.02, ROW_Y[i], lw=0.5)

ax.text(ex + ew / 2, 0.18, "×7 Objectives", fontsize=5.5, fontweight="bold",
        color="#666", ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)

# ── Embedding vectors ──
emb_x, emb_w, emb_h = 2.55, 0.18, 0.22
emb_labels = [r"$\mathbf{h_1}$", r"$\mathbf{h_2}$", r"$\mathbf{h_k}$"]

for i, lab in enumerate(emb_labels):
    ey = ROW_Y[i] - emb_h / 2
    ns = 5
    sh = emb_h / ns
    for j in range(ns):
        f = j / (ns - 1)
        r = int(0x00 + (0x7B - 0x00) * f)
        g = int(0x72 + (0x68 - 0x72) * f)
        b_ = int(0xB2 + (0xAE - 0xB2) * f)
        ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((emb_x, ey + j * sh), emb_w, sh,
            fc=f"#{r:02X}{g:02X}{b_:02X}", ec="none", zorder=4))
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((emb_x, ey), emb_w, emb_h,
        boxstyle="round,pad=0.01", fc="none", ec=C_PURPLE, lw=0.6, zorder=5))
    ax.text(emb_x + emb_w / 2, ROW_Y[i], lab, fontsize=7, color="white",
            ha="center", va="center", zorder=6,
            path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=1.5, foreground="#333")])
    arr(ex + ew + 0.02, ROW_Y[i], emb_x - 0.02, ROW_Y[i], lw=0.5)

ax.text(emb_x + emb_w / 2, 0.18, "frozen [CLS]", fontsize=4.5, color=C_GRAY,
        ha="center", va="center", style="italic", zorder=5)

# ── t→ temporal label ──
ax.text(3.10, ROW_Y[0] + 0.12, r"$t \rightarrow$", fontsize=8, color="#555",
        ha="center", va="center", zorder=5, fontweight="bold")

# ── BiGRU ──
gru_x, gru_w, gru_h = 3.62, 0.82, 0.78
gru_y = ROW_Y[1] - gru_h / 2

rbox(gru_x, gru_y, gru_w, gru_h, fc="#ECE4F5", ec=C_PURPLE, lw=0.6, z=3)
ax.text(gru_x + gru_w / 2, gru_y + gru_h - 0.12, "BiGRU", fontsize=8.5,
        fontweight="bold", color=C_PURPLE, ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)

fwd_y = gru_y + 0.30
bwd_y = fwd_y + 0.12
arr(gru_x + 0.10, fwd_y, gru_x + gru_w - 0.10, fwd_y, c=C_BLUE, lw=1.0)
bwd = FancyArrowPatch((gru_x + gru_w - 0.10, bwd_y), (gru_x + 0.10, bwd_y),
    arrowstyle="-|>", color="#5B4A8E", lw=1.0, mutation_scale=6, zorder=6)
bwd.set_path_effects([pe.withStroke(linewidth=2.0, foreground="white")])
ax.add_patch(bwd)

for j in range(3):
    sx = gru_x + 0.10 + j * 0.22
    ax.add_patch(FancyBboxPatch((sx, gru_y + 0.06), 0.15, 0.11,
        boxstyle="round,pad=0.02", fc="#D8CEE8", ec=C_PURPLE, lw=0.2, zorder=4, alpha=0.7))

targets_y = [gru_y + gru_h * 0.80, gru_y + gru_h * 0.50, gru_y + gru_h * 0.20]
for i in range(3):
    arr(emb_x + emb_w + 0.02, ROW_Y[i], gru_x - 0.02, targets_y[i], lw=0.5)

# ── MLP ──
mlp_x, mlp_w, mlp_h = 4.72, 0.42, 0.50
mlp_y = gru_y + (gru_h - mlp_h) / 2

rbox(mlp_x, mlp_y, mlp_w, mlp_h, fc="#F0EDE8", ec="#B5A99A", lw=0.5, z=3)
ax.text(mlp_x + mlp_w / 2, mlp_y + mlp_h / 2, "MLP", fontsize=8,
        fontweight="bold", color="#5A4E3F", ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)

arr(gru_x + gru_w + 0.02, gru_y + gru_h / 2,
    mlp_x - 0.02, mlp_y + mlp_h / 2, lw=0.6)

# ── Output (centered text, no icon overlap) ──
out_x, out_w, out_h = 5.45, 0.55, 0.22

jb_y = mlp_y + mlp_h / 2 + 0.06
rbox(out_x, jb_y, out_w, out_h, fc="#FDEDEA", ec=C_CORAL, lw=0.6, z=3)
ax.text(out_x + out_w / 2, jb_y + out_h / 2, "Jailbreak", fontsize=6.5,
        fontweight="bold", color=C_CORAL, ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)

bn_y = mlp_y + mlp_h / 2 - 0.06 - out_h
rbox(out_x, bn_y, out_w, out_h, fc="#E8F5F0", ec=C_TEAL, lw=0.6, z=3)
ax.text(out_x + out_w / 2, bn_y + out_h / 2, "Benign", fontsize=6.5,
        fontweight="bold", color=C_TEAL, ha="center", va="center", zorder=5)

arr(mlp_x + mlp_w + 0.02, mlp_y + mlp_h / 2 + 0.06,
    out_x - 0.02, jb_y + out_h / 2, lw=0.5)
arr(mlp_x + mlp_w + 0.02, mlp_y + mlp_h / 2 - 0.06,
    out_x - 0.02, bn_y + out_h / 2, lw=0.5)

ax.text(4.95, 0.55, "shared across all 7 variants", fontsize=4.5,
        color=C_GRAY, ha="center", va="center", style="italic", zorder=5)

# ══════════════════════════════
# SAVE
# ══════════════════════════════
out_dir = "/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0514_2/projects/persuasion_turn_jailbreak_detect/figures/paper"
for path, dpi in [(f"{out_dir}/fig1_architecture.png", 300),
                   (f"{out_dir}/fig1_architecture.pdf", None),
                   ("/tmp/fig_optimize/fig1_v5.png", 300)]:
    kw = dict(bbox_inches="tight", facecolor=C_BG, pad_inches=0.05)
    if dpi:
        kw["dpi"] = dpi
    plt.savefig(path, **kw)
plt.close()
print("Done: fig1 v5")

1	% introduction.tex
2	
3	\section{Introduction}
4	
5	Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns. Crescendo~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo}, Foot-in-the-Door~\citep{fitd2024}, and Deceptive Delight~\citep{deceptivedelight2024} all rely on persuasion as their core mechanism: \citet{zeng2024pap} catalogue 40 persuasion techniques across jailbreak families, and \citet{hagendorff2026reasoning} identify strategies in 97\% of successful attacks. Because individual attack turns occupy the same embedding region as benign text~\citep{bullwinkel2025repeng}, no single-turn filter can distinguish them from legitimate conversation.
6	
7	Existing defenses leave a critical gap. Production classifiers such as Llama Guard~\citep{inan2023llamaguard}, WildGuard~\citep{han2024wildguard}, and ShieldGemma~\citep{zeng2024shieldgemma} operate on individual turns and miss multi-turn manipulation; Llama Guard~3 detects only 1.8\% of multi-turn jailbreaks in our evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:decomposition}). Multi-turn defenses (DeepContext~\citep{deepcontext2026}, BIID~\citep{tong2025biid}, G-Guard~\citep{gguard2025}) model conversation-level structure but each evaluates on a single attack family. None answers the central question: \emph{what representation properties enable a detector to generalize across attack families it has never seen?}
8	
9	Pretrained language understanding does not suffice at base model scale: vanilla DeBERTa-v3~\citep{he2021deberta} with temporal aggregation (cf.\ DeepContext) drops from F1\,=\,1.000 in-distribution to 0.312 on OOD Deceptive Delight, and GPT-5.5 reaches only 0.191--0.449 F1 (across prefix lengths) with 30--47\% unparseable responses (Appendix~\ref{sec:llm_judge}). The bottleneck is distributional: cross-attack generalization at base model scale benefits substantially from domain adaptation.
10	
11	Our pipeline, \textbf{DisPeD} (Disentangled Persuasion Detection)\footnote{We use `disentangled' to describe our experimental methodology of isolating individual factors through controlled ablation, distinct from disentangled representation learning ($\beta$-VAE, InfoGAN).}, separates encoder adaptation (Stage~1) from temporal classification (Stage~2, a frozen BiGRU; Figure~\ref{fig:architecture}). Seven Stage~1 variants each isolate a single factor while holding all others constant (Section~\ref{sec:method}); the contribution is the decomposition, not the pipeline.
12	
13	\begin{figure}[t]
14	\centering
15	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/paper/fig1_architecture.pdf}
16	\caption{DisPeD architecture. Stage~1 adapts a DeBERTa encoder on jailbreak conversation text (seven variant objectives). Stage~2 aggregates frozen \texttt{[CLS]} embeddings via BiGRU for conversation-level jailbreak detection. Only user turns are processed.}
17	\label{fig:architecture}
18	\end{figure}
19	
20	Controlled ablation across DeBERTa-v3 and RoBERTa~\citep{liu2019roberta} on four attack families and two training compositions shows that for base-size encoders, classification-based adaptation is the most robust variant on synthetic multi-turn OOD attacks. MLM collapses on mixed-LLM training (F1\,=\,0.289 $\approx$ vanilla) while classification DAPT maintains 0.818; RoBERTa-large (355M) handles ActorAttack~\citep{ren2024actorattack} without adaptation.
21	
22	While domain-adaptive pretraining generally improves downstream NLP tasks~\citep{gururangan2020dontstop}, three findings in our safety-detection setting are unexpected: (i)~classification DAPT outperforms vanilla by over 60 percentage points on OOD detection (and MLM by $\sim$50\,pp under mixed-LLM training)---the classification objective itself, not just domain exposure, drives the OOD benefit; (ii)~scrambled labels match correct labels for template-attack detection, suggesting the classification objective's benefit is independent of label semantics; and (iii)~this hierarchy reverses entirely on human-authored data, revealing condition-specific rather than universal advantages of supervised adaptation.
23	
24	Our contributions:
